timing: The 5 October calculator-to-planner change needs its 28-day observation window through 2 November. Review finalized GSC data through 2 November before deciding to apply this proposal. No rollout or reminder is scheduled.
hypothesis: Explicit m³ and 20kg bag outputs, with a clear bag-material-only cost description, may improve search intent matching. Current metadata already describes dimensions and bags, so improvement is unproven.
scope: Title, meta description, matching Open Graph fields, visible introduction and WebApplication description. This is a combined snippet/content test, not an isolated title experiment. No formulas, prices, yields, canonicals, H1 or tracking changes.

evidence.source: Finalized Google Search Console web search, page dimension; GA4 event report
evidence.limitations: Click counts are small; average position and query mix changed. Event counts are repeated interactions, not people. Initial evidence is a hypothesis, not a causal diagnosis.

apply_after_review: Follow AGENTS.md and the site growth skill; start clean and current on main.
Refresh the finalized 28-day baseline, recent changes and indexing evidence. Keep this unapplied if evidence no longer supports it.
Update only the slab URL's sitemap lastmod to the actual rollout date.
Run every required validation command and desktop/mobile slab and privacy checks before committing and pushing.
Record the actual deployment date and mark this proposal applied in the same commit.
evaluation: Record the first observed Google recrawl after deployment; Google may rewrite titles and snippets.
Compare 28 complete post-recrawl days with the refreshed 28-day baseline. Allow GSC finalization delay.
Review clicks, impressions, CTR and average position together; use comparable query/device/country slices only where rows and sample sizes are sufficient.
Check organic landing sessions, distinct calculation users and sessions with calculator_complete rather than treating raw events as conversions.
Avoid retuning during the observation window except for a correctness, indexing, accessibility or clear regression fix.
Treat inconclusive results as inconclusive; this before/after comparison is not a randomized experiment.
